patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive disinhibition, compulsive behaviors, and personality change in a previously reserved school principal.
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. V. is a 62-year-old right-handed Hispanic woman referred by her son for progressive personality changes over 2 years. He reports that his mother, formerly a reserved and professional school principal known for her decorum, began making inappropriate remarks at school board meetings approximately 2 years ago. She was eventually asked to retire early. Over the past year, her behavior has escalated markedly. She makes crude sexual jokes to strangers, has been found shoplifting small items (which she denies), and has made repeated unwanted advances toward a neighbor. She has developed compulsive behavior around food — she will eat continuously and has started eating food off other people's plates without permission. She also has a new compulsion to arrange objects in her kitchen in precise patterns for hours. Her son has found evidence of online gambling, spending over $8,000 in six months. She expresses no concern about any of this, stating she is 'finally doing what she wants.' She complains of no depressive symptoms, hallucinations, or pain. Neurological review of systems otherwise negative.

clinical_assessment.impression: 3 of the six Rascovsky behavioural features are documented, against the three required for possible behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia, alongside a dysexecutive bedside profile. The diagnosis is behavioural and is made on this assessment; imaging supports it and does not substitute for it. Memory and visuospatial function are relatively spared, which is the discriminator against Alzheimer's disease and the reason a screening total alone understates the syndrome.

output.query: behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia management pharmacological nonpharmacological

results.title: Pharmacological management of frontal-network neurodegenerative syndromes
results.finding: SSRIs (sertraline, fluvoxamine) may reduce compulsive and disinhibited behaviours; limited RCT evidence

results.title: Trazodone in frontal-network neurodegeneration
results.finding: Trazodone 100-300 mg/day reduces agitation and improves sleep in frontal-network neurodegenerative syndromes (Lebert et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2004)

results.title: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors in frontal-network neurodegeneration
results.finding: No benefit demonstrated; may worsen behavioural symptoms due to acetylcholinergic-serotonergic imbalance

output.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for the frontotemporal lobar degeneration syndromes; management is symptomatic. SSRIs (sertraline, fluvoxamine) have modest evidence for reducing compulsive and disinhibited behaviors; evidence is largely from small trials and open-label studies. Trazodone has randomized controlled trial evidence for reducing agitation and improving sleep (Lebert et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2004). Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors have not demonstrated benefit and may worsen behavioral symptoms in these patients.

interactions: Levothyroxine + sertraline: monitor thyroid function as SSRIs may alter thyroid hormone metabolism
warnings: Monitor for SSRI-associated hyponatremia in elderly female patients
alternatives: Trazodone 50-100mg at bedtime for agitation and sleep

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic

differential.key_features: Behavioral-predominant AD can mimic bvFTD; expect posterior parietal involvement and amyloid positivity — rebut with FDG/amyloid biomarkers.

differential.diagnosis: Primary psychiatric disorder (late-onset bipolar, personality change)
differential.key_features: No psychiatric history before age 62; the absence of prior episodes and the presence of frontal atrophy/release signs argue for a neurodegenerative cause.
Vascular risk factors may be present but MRI/FDG pattern is degenerative-lobar, not strategic infarct or extensive small-vessel ischaemic burden.
No classic triad (gait apraxia, urinary incontinence, cognitive decline) and ventriculomegaly is commensurate with atrophy.
No fasciculations, bulbar dysfunction, or limb weakness on exam.

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral frontal and/or anterior temporal atrophy in a lobar pattern with relative posterior sparing

optimal_actions.expected_finding: No reversible metabolic or infectious cause of cognitive decline identified

optimal_actions.action: Order comprehensive neuropsychological battery characterising executive function, social cognition, language and memory
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-executive and social-cognition deficits with relative sparing of episodic memory and visuospatial function

optimal_actions.action: Search medical literature for behavioural variant ftd diagnostic criteria
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirms Rascovsky 2011 criteria, FDG-PET evidence (Foster 2007), and management approach (Bang 2015)

optimal_actions.action: Consult behavioral/cognitive neurology for syndromic diagnosis, biomarker interpretation, and longitudinal care plan
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Behavioral neurology confirms bvFTD syndrome, coordinates biomarkers and disclosure

optimal_actions.action: Order FDG-PET brain to characterise frontotemporal hypometabolism and distinguish bvFTD from AD
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bifrontal and/or anterior temporal hypometabolism with relative posterior sparing
optimal_actions.guideline_source: Foster 2007 FDG-PET in FTD vs AD

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identifies or excludes pathogenic C9orf72 / GRN / MAPT variant relevant to prognosis and cascade testing

optimal_actions.guideline_source: Foster 2007 FDG-PET in FTD vs AD

optimal_actions.action: Discuss symptomatic SSRI for behavioural symptoms and verify safety against current regimen
optimal_actions.expected_finding: SSRI such as sertraline appropriate; AChE inhibitors and high-dose benzodiazepines flagged

optimal_actions.action: Perform a structured behavioural and cognitive assessment with informant history, scored against the six behavioural features of the Rascovsky criteria — disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, perseverative or compulsive behaviour, dietary change, and a dysexecutive profile with relative sparing of memory and visuospatial function — and record how many are present
optimal_actions.expected_finding: At least three of the six behavioural features documented from the informant history, with a dysexecutive profile and relatively spared memory and visuospatial function

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

sequence_constraints.reason: Exclude structural cause of focal cognitive symptoms and screen for elevated ICP before lumbar puncture.

critical_actions: Document evolution of personality and behavioural change from family informant given patient's anosognosia.
Address financial decision-making and any active fiduciary roles given documented impulsivity.
Apply Rascovsky 2011 bvFTD criteria explicitly (≥3 of 6 core features within 3 years) and document functional decline.
Assess and document decision-making, financial, and driving capacity given the high risk of impulsivity and impaired judgment in FTD.
Provide caregiver education, safety planning, and referral to FTD-focused support resources.
Offer genetic counselling and discuss cascade testing options if a pathogenic variant is identified or suspected.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Do not start memantine: no evidence of benefit in bvFTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
key_reasoning_points: Disinhibition, compulsive behaviors, loss of empathy, and executive dysfunction satisfy Rascovsky criteria.
Imaging shows the lobar atrophy and frontotemporal hypometabolism pattern expected of FTLD.
Mild rigidity without bradykinesia or rest tremor does not justify DaTscan in this presentation.
Negative amyloid biomarkers exclude AD as the underlying pathology.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Could prompt DaTscan for suspected parkinsonism.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild extrapyramidal features are common in advanced bvFTD; DaTscan is not indicated.
